Beyond the stile stands an attractive row of riverside trees – alder, hazel, beech, hawthorn and ash. Go across to the far corner of a field, where a through-stile gives onto a small, lightly wooded hill,[…]

glosses: To provide a view of.

examples.text: His window gave the park.
Columbus dwellers of Woodland Meadow Apts may not find themselves in a perfectly bucolic setting, as the residential complex gives onto a military defense logistics ground.

glosses: To exhibit as a product or result; to produce; to yield.

examples.text: The number of men, divided by the number of ships, gives four hundred to each ship.

glosses: To cause; to make; used with the infinitive.

examples.text: But there the duke was given to understand / That in a gondola were seen together / Lorenzo and his amorous Jessica.

glosses: To cause (someone) to have; produce in (someone); effectuate.

examples.text: "Can do" gives me a choice, while "should do" gives me a complex.

glosses: To allow or admit by way of supposition; to concede.

examples.text: He can be bad-tempered, I'll give you that, but he's a hard worker.
I give not heaven for lost.

glosses: To attribute; to assign; to adjudge.

examples.text: I don't wonder at people giving him to me for a lover.

glosses: To communicate or announce (advice, tidings, etc.); to pronounce or utter (an opinion, a judgment, a shout, etc.).

examples.text: The umpire finally gave his decision: the ball was out.

glosses: To grant power, permission, destiny, etc. (especially to a person); to allot; to allow.

examples.text: These are the statutes and judgments, which ye shall observe to do in the land, which the Lord God of thy fathers giveth thee to possess it, all the days that ye live upon the earth.

once again
'Tis given me to behold my friend.
Then give thy friend to shed the sacred wine.

glosses: To devote or apply (oneself).

examples.text: The soldiers give themselves to plunder.
That boy is given to fits of bad temper.

glosses: To become soft or moist.

examples.text: Some moyst weather hath‥caused the powder to give and danke.

glosses: To shed tears; to weep.

examples.text: Whose eyes do never give / But through lust and laughter.

glosses: To have a misgiving.

examples.text: My mind gives ye're reserv'd / To rob poor market women.

glosses: The amount of bending that something undergoes when a force is applied to it; a tendency to yield under pressure; resilience.

examples.text: This chair doesn't have much give.
There is no give in his dogmatic religious beliefs.
The striker's job was onerous, too, because there was so little "give" in the metal, and the perpetual jarring was indeed trying to the muscles.
